title: [Attention] Add FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE backend for Hopper sparse MLA (#46189)
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a Python-only `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` backend for sparse MLA
models on Hopper GPUs. The backend reuses vLLM's existing FlashAttention MLA
wrapper and sparse MLA index conversion path, then calls
`flash_attn_varlen_func(..., fa_version=3)` for BF16 KV-cache sparse decode.

The tested GLM-5.1-FP8 checkpoint has:

- `num_attention_heads = 64`
- `kv_lora_rank = 512`
- `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`
- compressed KV dim = `576`
- `index_topk = 2048`
- FP8 weight quantization, with BF16 KV cache in this backend

The vLLM reference serving configuration for this checkpoint uses tensor
parallel size 8. Under that configuration, the query head count is
`64 / 8 = 8`. The current vLLM FlashMLA sparse implementation, following
upstream FlashMLA kernel constraints, **supports only `q_head = 64` on Hopper**. When
GLM-5.1-FP8 runs with TP8, the local `q_head` is 8, so the current **path pads it
to 64 before running the sparse attention kernel**. On Blackwell, the FlashMLA sparse kernel constraint is `q_head = 128`. This PR does not add Blackwell support.

Code references:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`: `prefill_padding` is set
  to 64 on Hopper and 128 on Blackwell.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`: for BF16 KV cache,
  `_forward_bf16_kv()` calls `_bf16_flash_mla_kernel()` for the token batch,
  including decode tokens; that kernel pads `q` to `self.prefill_padding`
  before calling `flash_mla_sparse_fwd()`.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py`: for FP8 KV-cache decode,
  `_fp8_flash_mla_kernel()` separately pads `q` to 64 or 128 before calling
  `flash_mla_with_kvcache()`.

## Related PRs and Issues

Relevant open work:

- [#39924: `[Attention] Add FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE backend`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39924)
  - Status: open.
  - This targets FA4 DSA support on Blackwell through upstream
    FlashAttention DSA support. This PR targets Hopper/SM90 and reuses vLLM's
    existing FA3 wrapper path, so it is not the same implementation target, but maybe can be combined together.
- [#39941: `[Attention][SM90] Add CUTLASS FA3 sparse MLA attention backend for Hopper GPUs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39941)
  - Status: open.
  - This is another Hopper sparse MLA direction, but it adds a separate
    CUTLASS-based extension and kernel wrapper. This PR is Python-only and
    routes through the existing vLLM FlashAttention wrapper.
- [#34744: `[WIP][Attention] Enable masked MHA for topk sparse attention using FA4`](htt …[truncated]

title: [ROCm] Fix OOB During Model Warmup With `ROCM_ATTN` and MRV2 (#46548)
linked_issues: #46179 [Bug]: `vllm serve neuralmagic/Llama-3.2-1B-quantized.w8a8` Failing On ROCm w/ MRV2
body:
Resolves https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46179 (as well as numerous other failing tests in AMD CI, e.g. `pytest -v -s tests/compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py::test_full_graph[neuralmagic/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic-model_kwargs1-2]`).

This PR resolves a latent seg fault in the `ROCM_ATTN` that was exposed when Llama was added to the default architectures for MRV2 in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43458.

The seg fault manifests when the kernel tries to read one-past the query row here:
```
Qlocal[h] = q_ptrh8[qhead_idx * HEAD_SIZE / 8 + qhead_elemh8];
```
It's exposed with V2 enabled because warmup happens with `num_seqs=1024`. We just need to ensure that `qhead_elemh8` is clamped so that the surplus lanes don't try to access OOB memory. We just populate them with the last valid qhead value, which is arbitrary since those values don't get fed to the accumulated output.

I've reverted https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46180 as part of this fix.

cc @mawong-amd (and credit to him for assisting with this!)

title: [Bugfix] FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 compatibility with GLM-5 NVFP4 (#46506)
body:
Models with an index_topk skip pattern (e.g. GLM-5.2, index_topk_freq=4)
build a sparse-MLA indexer only on a subset of backbone layers; the
remaining "skip" layers are constructed with indexer=None and instead
receive the shared top-k indices buffer via MLAAttention
(extra_impl_args["topk_indices_buffer"], see mla_attention.py).

FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 asserted `indexer is not None` and only read
`indexer.topk_indices_buffer`, so every skip layer crashed at init with
"requires a sparse-MLA indexer". This broke serving of GLM-5.2 (both
NVFP4 and MXFP4) on SM120, even though MLAAttention already passes the
shared buffer for these layers.

Mirror FLASHMLA_SPARSE: take the shared buffer from the indexer when
present, otherwise from mla_args. The existing
`assert self.topk_indices_buffer is not None` still guards the
truly-missing case.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass num_kv_splits to aiter mla_reduce_v1 (#46760)
body:
## Purpose

#46692 bumped AITER to `v0.1.16.post2`, which includes ROCm/aiter#3391. That aiter PR added a **required `num_kv_splits` argument** to `mla_reduce_v1` (now position 7 of the registered op schema). The FP8 ASM prefill reduce call in the AITER dense MLA backend (`rocm_aiter_mla.py`) was not updated, so on `main` today the `out_3d` Tensor is bound to the `num_kv_splits` (int) slot and **every MLA model crashes at prefill on gfx950** (DeepSeek-R1-0528, Kimi-K2.6, and their MXFP4 variants):

```
RuntimeError: aiter::mla_reduce_v1() Expected a value of type 'int' for argument 'num_kv_splits' but instead found type 'Tensor'.
Declaration: aiter::mla_reduce_v1(Tensor partial_output, Tensor partial_lse, Tensor reduce_indptr,
  Tensor? reduce_final_map, Tensor reduce_partial_map, SymInt max_seqlen_q, SymInt num_kv_splits,
  Tensor final_output, Tensor? final_lse=None) -> ()
```

**Fix:** pass `0` for `num_kv_splits`. The kernel uses `params.max_splits = max(cu_num, num_kv_splits)`, so `0` reproduces the **exact pre-#3391 behavior** (`max(cu_num, 0) == cu_num`). This matches what aiter's own caller (`aiter/mla.py`) and op test (`op_tests/test_mla_prefill_ps.py`) pass for this prefill-PS reduce path.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches the `num_kv_splits` / `mla_reduce_v1` caller (checked via `gh pr list --search`). SGLang hit the identical break: ROCm/aiter#3689.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Add AITER FlashAttention MLA prefill backend (`ROCM_AITER_FA`) (#45033)
body:
## Summary

Adds an AITER-backed MLA prefill backend that calls `aiter.flash_attn_varlen_func`
directly instead of falling back to the upstream CK-tile FlashAttention path on ROCm.

It dispatches the fast `aiter::fmha_fwd_*` kernel on gfx950 and, unlike the CK
fallback, needs **no V padding** (native qk=192 / v=128 head dims) and returns
`softmax_lse` already shaped `(nheads, total_q)` (**no LSE transpose**). This is the
fp16/bf16 generic-varlen prefill path; it is auto-selected on gfx950 and transparently
falls back to `FLASH_ATTN` everywhere else.

Applies to all MLA models on gfx950 (DeepSeek V3/R1, Kimi-K2, …); validated on
`amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4-AttnFP8` and `deepseek-ai/Deepseek-V3`.

## What changed

- **New** `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/aiter_flash_attn.py` —
  `AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend` (`get_name() == "ROCM_AITER_FA"`), implementing
  `run_prefill_new_tokens` (causal) and `run_prefill_context_chunk` (unmasked).
- **`registry.py`** — registers the `ROCM_AITER_FA` enum member.
- **`selector.py`** — on ROCm, prefers `[ROCM_AITER_FA, FLASH_ATTN]`.

## Selection & gating

- Auto-selected only when **all** hold: `current_platform.is_rocm()`, `on_gfx950()`,
  `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, and `aiter.flash_attn_varlen_func` is importable.
- `validate_configuration` filters it out on non-gfx950 / aiter-missing hosts, so those
  fall back to `FLASH_ATTN` with no behavior change.
- Precision follows the inherited `supported_dtypes = [float16, bfloat16]` 
- Can be forced explicitly via `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'`.

## Performance

**Models:** `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4-AttnFP8` (TP4) and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` (TP8),
both on gfx950.
**Method:** baseline (`FLASH_ATTN`/CK) vs new (`ROCM_AITER_FA`) forced via
`--attention-config` in the same image — only the MLA-prefill backend differs.
`--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` is used so prompts are chunked and the chunked-context
extend path (what this PR changes) is exercised. `vllm bench serve`, random dataset,
`--ignore-eos`.

title: [Model] Add support for openai/privacy-filter (#41026)
body:
## Purpose

Adds support for [`openai/privacy-filter`](https://huggingface.co/openai/privacy-filter) (`OpenAIPrivacyFilterForTokenClassification`): a gpt-oss-style MoE encoder (GQA 14/2, YaRN RoPE, 128 experts top-4, attention sinks) repurposed as a bidirectional token classifier for PII detection. Every layer uses non-causal attention with a banded ±`sliding_window` mask. The LM head is replaced with a 33-class BIOES score head.

The new model reuses gpt-oss by making the implementation more flexible (sliding window policy, NeoX / GPT-J RoPE style). `GptOssForCausalLM` behavior is unchanged.

Two preliminary fixes are bundled in:

- `flash_attn.py`: `_forward_encoder_attention()` omitted `s_aux=self.sinks` while the decoder path passes it, so encoder layers with sinks silently dropped them.
- `fused_moe/oracle/unquantized.py`: `flashinfer_cutlass_moe` aliases `SWIGLUOAI` to plain `Swiglu` on the unquantized branch. Demote both FlashInfer backends when `activation==SWIGLUOAI` so Triton's `swigluoai_and_mul` is chosen (same pattern as the Qwen3.5/`dp_size` demotion just above).

AI-assisted, every line reviewed and tested by the submitter. `gh search` for `OpenAIPrivacyFilter`, `openai_privacy_filter`, `privacy-filter`, and `banded attention` returned no duplicates.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_token_classification.py -k privacy -v
```

Seven prompts covering all eight PII categories, compared against `AutoModelForTokenClassification`.

## Test Result

H100, bf16:

- 7/7 prompts within `atol=0.1, rtol=1e-2` (max softmax diff: 0.099).
- 91/91 token argmax match vs HF.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix LSE log-base mismatch in DCP + FlashInfer MLA decode (#47079)
body:
## Purpose

FlashInfer's trtllm-gen MLA decode kernel returns LSE in **log2** (per flashinfer's own reference at `flashinfer/trace/templates/attention.py:81`: `logsumexp / log(2.0)`), but `MLAAttention`'s DCP combine in `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py` hard-codes `is_lse_base_on_e=True` when calling `cp_lse_ag_out_rs` / `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce`, asserting natural log. The mismatch makes the per-shard re-weighting use the wrong base when combining DCP partial attention outputs, producing incorrect softmax denominators and corrupted attention values.

This is the residual bug after #43729 ("Support DCP with FlashInfer MLA") merged: that PR wired LSE *return* through `FlashInferMLAImpl` (so DCP combine now runs), but left the combine assuming natural-log LSE.

**Symptom** on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 + FP8 KV + DCP=4 + `FLASHINFER_MLA`:
- Same prompt sent twice within one run produces different argmax tokens at 24/32 positions (vs ~4/32 noise floor on the no-DCP baseline with the same backend).
- Argmax tokens diverge from the no-DCP baseline on every test prompt.
- `TRITON_MLA`, FlashAttention MLA, FlashMLA, and Cutlass MLA are unaffected — their kernels emit LSE in natural log, matching the old hard-coded assumption.

**Fix:** declare each backend's LSE base as a capability flag (`lse_base_on_e`) on `AttentionImplBase` (default `True` / natural log), override it to `False` on `FlashInferMLAImpl`, and thread it through the DCP combine. The kernels already support both bases natively via their `IS_BASE_E` constexpr (`tl.exp/tl.log` vs `tl.exp2/tl.log2`), so there is no FP multiply or rounding loss — and adding another log2-emitting backend later is a one-line `ClassVar` instead of a call-site edit.

## Not a duplicate

- **#43729** (merged) added FlashInfer MLA + DCP support and the LSE-return plumbing, but not this log-base reconciliation.
- **#47074** ("Use larger workspace size for Flashinfer MLA LSE") touches the same file but fixes an orthogonal issue — a `trtllm_gen_softmax_workspace` allocation overflow — not the LSE base. The two are complementary.

## Test Plan & Results

Verified end-to-end on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 + DCP=4 + FP8 KV (Blackwell GB200) against a TEP4 (no DCP, same FlashInfer backend) baseline:

- **5-prompt greedy-decode refcomp** (max_tokens=32, top_p=1): **0 token mismatches** after fix vs `28+24+24+4+0` before; within-run stability `24/32 → 5/32` (matches baseline `4/32`).

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MLA] Pass q/kv dtypes to get_mla_metadata_v1 in FP8 decode (#46997)
body:
## Purpose

Fix a silent accuracy regression for MLA models served with an **FP8 KV cache** on **gfx950 (MI355X)** using the AITER MLA backend. With `amd-aiter == 0.1.16.post2`, Kimi-K2.5 at TP2 (32 q-heads/rank) produces garbage — gsm8k drops from ~0.93 to ~0.

### Root cause

`AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` builds the persistent split/reduce metadata for decode via `get_mla_metadata_v1`, but did **not** forward `dtype_q` / `dtype_kv` (they default to `None`). For the gfx950 fp8/fp8 `nhead=32`, `qlen=1` internal "fold-to-16" decode path, omitting the dtypes makes `get_mla_metadata_v1` emit **wrong split/reduce metadata**, which silently corrupts the decode output.

Note that `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` (which sizes the metadata buffers, a few lines above) was already given `q_dtype` / `kv_dtype`. This change makes the two metadata APIs consistent by passing the same dtypes to `get_mla_metadata_v1`.

This is a different fix from #46952. #46952 works around the symptom by padding the q head count `32 -> 64` so the (broken) fold path is avoided entirely; this PR fixes the root cause so the metadata for the fold path is correct. The fix is 6 lines and reuses values already computed in `__init__`.

### Affected configurations

Triggered by **gfx950 + FP8 KV cache + per-rank head count that takes the nhead->16 fold path** (verified: 32, i.e. TP2). bf16 KV cache and the native head counts (16/64/128) are unaffected; this change always forwards the dtypes, which is a no-op for paths that already worked.

## Test Plan

End-to-end, Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950), FP8 KV cache, TP2 (32 heads/rank):

```bash
vllm serve /shareddata/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4 -tp 2 \
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling

    --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 3
```

body:
Depends on: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46167 and https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/150

## Description
This is the first PR in a broader CuTeDSL warmup series. The initial study focuses only on the FA4 MLA prefill path.

This PR adds a generic CuTeDSL warmup hook and one provider for FA4 MLA prefill. The goal is to compile the relevant FA4 CuTeDSL kernels during model warmup, before serving real requests, so runtime inference does not pay JIT latency spikes.

The warmup flow is provider-based:
1. CuTeDSL warmup runs from the GPU worker after regular kernel warmup and before CUDA graph capture.
2. Each supported kernel/provider can expose its own `get_cutedsl_warmup_plan`.
3. The provider inspects the active model/runtime config and returns compile-only units for the shapes/configs relevant to that setup.
4. Warmup deduplicates units by compile key.
5. Each compile unit is invoked with empty synthetic tensors matching the expected metadata, dtype, device, rank, and shape.

title: [Bugfix] Don't read KV cache past `seq_len` in triton paged attn kernels (#47305)
body:
The Triton unified_attention and ROCm paged-decode kernels load KV cache slots beyond seq_len (the unwritten tail of the last partial block) and rely on the score mask to drop them. That is unsafe when the tail is non-finite: masked positions get softmax weight 0, but 0 * NaN = NaN still poisons the output. In `compute_tile_loop_bounds` the causal-derived `max_seq_prefix_len` can additionally overshoot seq_len for non-causal (cross-)attention, widening the over-read.

- `triton_attention_helpers.compute_tile_loop_bounds`: clamp the non-causal / mixed / prefix branch to exactly `seq_len`.
- `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.kernel_paged_attention_2d`: bound the K/V loads to `seq_len` (other=0.0), matching the score mask.

Surfaced as Whisper cross-attention emitting garbage on ROCm once MRV2 made it the default model runner. The over-read only affects output when the unwritten tail is non-finite (NaN under MRV2 on ROCm; harmless zero under MRV1 and on CUDA via 0 * 0). Freed KV blocks are never re-zeroed, so correctness relies on never reading past seq_len. MRV2 (unlike MRV1) runs a dummy warmup forward; for encoder-decoder it has no encoder input, so cross-attn attends to zero keys - an empty softmax that yields NaN on the ROCm kernel - and that NaN lands in the block tails the first real request reuses. The fix is correct regardless, since reading beyond seq_len is never valid.

I will open a separate PR to improve the MRV2 warmup in encoder-decoder case.

Claude was used to help find this!

title: [ROCm][MLA] Fuse MLA q/kv RMSNorm + FP8 per-token quant in the FP8 attention path (#44977)
body:
## Summary

The `MLADualRMSNormFusionPass` fuses the paired `q_a_layernorm` +
`kv_a_layernorm` of MLA attention into AITER's `fused_qk_rmsnorm` HIP kernel, but
that fusion silently stops firing once attention is **FP8-quantized** — the
earlier `RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass` folds the q-side
`rms_norm → fp8 per-token quant` into a single
`rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_fused_dynamic_quant` op, so the q latent is no longer a bare
`rms_norm` and the symmetric BF16 dual pattern no longer matches. This PR
enables the dual fusion for the FP8 path by matching that asymmetric pair (q
per-token-quant + kv `rms_norm`) and lowering it to a new
`fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_per_token_quant` custom op, backed by AITER's
`fused_qk_rmsnorm_per_token_quant` kernel, so a **single** kernel launch replaces
the separate q (norm + FP8 per-token quant) and kv (norm) kernels:

```text
# FP8, before this PR (q norm+quant fused; kv still a separate rms_norm):
q_fp8, q_scale = rocm_aiter_rmsnorm_fused_dynamic_quant(q_c, q_weight, eps, fp8)
kv_normed      = rms_norm(kv_c, kv_weight, eps)          # bf16

# FP8, after this PR (single fused launch):
q_fp8, q_scale, kv_normed = fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_per_token_quant(
    q_c, q_weight, kv_c, kv_weight, eps1, eps2)
```

Only the *q* latent is FP8 per-token-quantized (it feeds the FP8 `q_b_proj`
GEMM, a single `(M, 1)` scale); the *kv* latent is RMS-normed and consumed by
attention as bf16. This matches the layout produced by the upstream norm+quant
fusion.

The pattern is registered **only** when the installed AITER actually exposes
`fused_qk_rmsnorm_per_token_quant` (guarded by
`check_aiter_fused_qk_rmsnorm_per_token_quant()`), so it is a no-op on older
AITER builds and on non-ROCm platforms. No new flag — it rides on the existing
`fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm` pass config (O1+ with AITER).

- `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`: add the `fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_per_token_quant`

- `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rocm_aiter_fusion.py`: add
  `MLADualRMSPerTokenQuantPattern` and register it in
  `MLADualRMSNormFusionPass` when the kernel is available.
- `tests/compile/passes/test_fuse_mla_dual_rms_norm.py`: add a test that the

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Keep image bidirectional attention within the sliding window (#47217)
body:
## Purpose

Gemma4 vision models that use blockwise bidirectional image attention
(`use_bidirectional_attention="vision"` → 12B, 26B-A4B, 31B) silently fell back
to **causal-only** attention over image tokens whenever a single image's
soft-token span exceeded the text sliding window (e.g. ~1100 soft tokens at
`max_soft_tokens=1120` vs `sliding_window=1024`). This degraded vision/OCR
quality — catastrophic on the encoder-free **12B** (no vision tower to
compensate, output collapsed into fragmented `...` text) and latent on the
tower-based 26B/31B.

The defect is backend-agnostic (the runner builds the ranges), so it affected
both TRITON_ATTN (A100/SM80) and FA4 (SM90/Hopper); the fix touches both kernels.

- **Root cause:** `GPUModelRunner` dropped the *entire* bidirectional
  `mm_prefix` range for an image when `(range_len > sliding_window)`, leaving
  those image tokens fully causal in the LM.
- **Intended behavior** (HF reference, https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46850): on local/sliding
  layers the bidirectional block is **clamped to** the sliding window —
  `(causal OR blockwise) AND sliding_window` — not dropped. Global/full-attention
  layers are causal-only (already handled in vLLM via
  `_clear_mm_prefix_for_full_attn_layers`).

### Fix (three parts, gated to Gemma4)

- **Runner:** gate the oversized-range skip on a new model capability flag
  `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window`. Models that bound `mm_prefix` in-kernel keep
  the full range; all other models keep the existing drop (default-unset).
- **Triton kernel (A100/SM80):** add an `MM_PREFIX_CLAMP_SW` `constexpr` to
  `compute_kv_seq_mask`; when set, AND each `mm_prefix` range with the
  sliding-window past-bound `(q - kv) < SLIDING_WINDOW` (equivalent to HF's
  `sliding_window_overlay`; future `kv` passes trivially). Plumbed
  `Attention → TritonAttentionImpl → unified_attention → kernel`. Default
  `False` is dead-code-eliminated, so other models/backends are byte-identical.
- **FA4 / FlashAttention kernel (SM90/Hopper):** Gemma4 is forced onto the
  FLASH_ATTN backend whenever FA4 is available and `max_head_dim ≤ 512`
  (`Gemma4Config.verify_and_update_config`), so the Triton clamp does not run
  there. FA4 builds its mask via a CuTe-DSL `mask_mod` that is the *sole*
  element mask (causal/window masking is off when a `mask_mod` is present), so
  the bidirectional block was not window-bounded. `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod`
  now takes an optional `sliding_window`; when set it ANDs each range with
  `(q_idx - kv_idx) < sliding_window` —  …[truncated]

## Summary

This PR adds explicit TritonAttention support for Unlimited-OCR's R-SWA decode
mask. The Triton path implements the mask with:

```python
if USE_R_SWA:
    prefix_len = tl.load(rswa_prefix_lens_ptr + seq_idx)
    in_prefix = seq_offset[None, :] < prefix_len

body:
# [ROCm] Disable persistent sparse-MLA kernel for chunked-prefill continuations

## Summary
Fixes #47042. GLM-4.6/4.5 / DeepSeek-V3.2-style sparse-MLA (DSA) models on ROCm
produce correct output up to ~20K tokens and then collapse into repetition /
garbage at longer contexts.

Root cause: the AITER **persistent MLA work-stealing kernel**
(`get_mla_metadata_v1` + the `work_meta_data` persistent path in
`aiter.mla.mla_decode_fwd`, enabled unconditionally for the sparse-MLA backend
in #41990) is **numerically wrong for multi-token (prefill) batches**. The
per-token error is small in isolation, but chunked prefill runs a request
through several forward passes and the error **compounds** through the KV cache
across passes/layers until long-context decode collapses.

This is why the failure is gated on **chunk count**, not context length:

| max-num-batched-tokens | 20K prompt | chunks | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8192 | 22K tok | 3 | garbage (0/10 needles) |
| 12288 | 22K tok | 2 | correct |
| 21504 | 22K tok | 2 | correct |
| 12288 | 33K tok | 3 | garbage |

The persistent kernel is correct for **pure decode** (`qseqlen==1`) and for
**fresh single-chunk prefills**. This patch gates it on batch shape: it falls
back to the (correct) non-persistent split-KV path whenever any request in the
batch is a chunked-prefill *continuation* — i.e. it has more than one query
token this step *and* part of its context was already computed in an earlier
chunk (`seq_len > query_len`). Decode and single-chunk prefills keep the
persistent performance path, so there is no decode throughput regression.

## Why this is not a duplicate
- #47404 ("Synchronize sparse MLA metadata before graph replay") touches the
  same file but fixes a *different* bug: a stale-metadata race during CUDA-graph
  replay. The bug here is a **numerical correctness** bug in the kernel itself —
  it reproduces with `--enforce-eager` / `-cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE` (no graph
  replay), so metadata-ordering is not involved.
- #41973 / #41990 is the feature that *enabled* the persistent path (the source
  of this regression), not a fix.
- No open PR references #47042.

## Isolated (kernel-only) reproduction
A standalone script (no vLLM/model) builds a sparse-MLA batch, regenerates the
persistent metadata via `get_mla_metadata_v1`, and compares the persistent
kernel and the non-persistent kernel against a torch fp32 reference:

```
N=  1 (decode):        persistent max_relerr=0.000   non-persistent=0.000  -> OK
N=512 (prefill batch): persistent max_relerr=7.15    non-persistent=0.108  -> PERSISTENT WRONG …[truncated]

body:
### Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47300

Gemma4 vision models emit total gibberish on the FlashAttention-4 (CuTeDSL, SM90) backend when the context is long (>=~1k tokens past the sliding window) and contains at least one image. The Triton backend produces correct output on the same input.

Root cause — two bugs in `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`):

- Missing sliding window constraint. The mask implemented `causal OR mm_prefix` instead of `(causal AND sliding_window) OR mm_prefix`. When `mask_mod` is present, `_resolve_causal_local_window` sets `causal=False, local=False`, which disables the kernel's built-in window enforcement — the `mask_mod` becomes the sole element-level mask. Since it lacked the sliding window term, non-image tokens attended to the full causal context instead of the configured window (1024 tokens for Gemma4), destroying attention distributions on any sequence longer than the window.
- Local `q_idx` instead of absolute position. The FA4 kernel passes `q_idx` as 0-based within the current prefill chunk, while `kv_idx` is absolute (0-based over the full KV cache). The causal term `kv_idx <= q_idx` and the mm_prefix range comparisons used raw `q_idx`, producing wrong masks whenever `seqlen_q != seqlen_k` (chunked prefill with prior context, multi-turn conversations).

#### Changes

- `_make_mm_prefix_mask_mod` now accepts `sliding_window_left: int | None` and enforces `(q_abs - kv_idx) < sw` on the causal term when non-None. Two separate `@cute.jit` branches (with/without window) avoid runtime branching in the CuTe DSL.
- Both branches compute `q_abs = q_idx + (seqlen_k - seqlen_q)` via `seqlen_info` and use it for all position comparisons (causal, window, mm_prefix ranges), matching the Triton reference path (`compute_kv_seq_mask`).
- Call site passes `1 + window_size[0]` (Triton convention) with a `>= 0` guard so global-attention layers (`-1, -1`) correctly get `sw_left=None` (causal-only, no window).

#### Scope

- Only affects models with `is_mm_prefix_lm=True` running on FA4 (SM90+).
- Global-attention layers (no sliding window) take the `else` branch — causal-only mask, no window. Behaviour matches the pre-fix code for these layers (plus the `q_abs` correction).
- Models without sliding window (bagel, molmo2, paligemma) get `sw_left=None` — causal-only branch. No change in behaviour beyond the `q_abs` fix.

title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 overflow in triton_decode_attention page offsets (#47671)
body:
## Purpose

`_fwd_kernel_stage1` / `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` load `kv_page_number` as int32 and multiply it by the KV buffer page stride in int32. With MLA c_kv (576 dims) and PAGE_SIZE 480 the page stride is ~276k, so page numbers above ~7.7k overflow to negative offsets → CUDA illegal memory access. Hybrid models hit this quickly: all layer groups share one block pool, so a 90GB KV buffer already holds ~163k pages. The error is async, so the reported stack typically blames an unrelated later kernel.

Fix: cast the page number to int64 after the load — the same pattern the other block-indexed triton kernels (fla `fused_recurrent`, `kda`, `causal_conv1d`) already use. C++ cache kernels use `int64_t` and CUTLASS_MLA is unaffected.

## Test Plan / Result

Reproduced with Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (TRITON_MLA) on GB200: a fixed-seed request loop crashed deterministically once allocated block ids crossed ~7767 (crash-site block ids spanned 7709–7778, straddling 2³¹/(480·576)); CUTLASS_MLA on the same trigger passed, isolating the kernel. With this cast the same loop passes all rounds, and gsm8k 5-shot greedy returns to baseline (strict-match 0.8704 vs 0.8711 baseline, 0 request errors; 285/1319 failed requests before the fix). `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes.

Note: the GPU validation ran on our development branch, where the identical cast was applied to the pre-refactor form of these lines; happy to rerun anything reviewers want on this exact branch.

## Duplicate check

No open PR/issue covers this: searched `triton_decode_attention`, `int32 overflow decode`, `kv_loc int64`. Closest is #45384 (int32 overflow in `concat_mla_q` warp index) — a different kernel and offset.

*AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for diagnosis and drafting; the change and tests were reviewed and run by the submitter.*

title: [Bugfix]Fix DeepSeek-V4 fp8_ds_mla KV cache reshape (#47716)
linked_issues: #47648 [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark fails on H200/SM90 with FlashMLA KV cache shape mismatch
body:
Fixes #47648.

DeepSeek-V4 FlashMLA uses a custom `fp8_ds_mla` KV layout with 584 bytes per token. The main MLA and SWA cache specs already carry `cache_dtype_str`, but they did not consistently expose `kv_quant_mode`, and the GPU model runner used the global cache dtype when computing backend KV cache shapes.

As a result, DSpark serving on H200 could allocate/reshape SWA KV cache as the semantic 512-byte head size, then fail in FlashMLA sparse decode with:

```text
RuntimeError: kv must have shape (num_blocks, page_block_size, h_kv, bytes_per_token)
```

This PR propagates `kv_quant_mode` for DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA specs and prefers the layer-local `cache_dtype_str` when computing KV cache shapes.

Co-discovered and validated with @yy-fighting.

## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark startup on H200/SM90 with FlashMLA when using `--spec-method dspark` and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

Before this change, the DeepSeek-V4 SWA KV cache could be reshaped as:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 512)
```

but FlashMLA expects the DeepSeek-V4 `fp8_ds_mla` layout:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)
```

## Test Plan

Tested on 4x H200 with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`.

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --spec-method dspark \
  --spec-model /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --spec-tokens 5 \
  --port 30004
```

Small serving benchmark:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30004 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model /data0/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 128 \
  --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 16 \
  --request-rate 4 \
  --max-concurrency 4 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

## Test Result

Before the fix, startup failed during DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA warmup:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 512)
RuntimeError: kv must have shape (num_blocks, page_block_size, h_kv, bytes_per_token)
```

After the fix, the cache shape is correct:

```text
swa_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)
kv_shape=(83520, 64, 1, 584)   # compress_ratio=4
kv_shape=(83520, 2, 1, 584)    # compress_ratio=128
```

```text

Graph capturing finished
/health -> 200
